question: In the CAJPA sample investment management RFP (Appendix Z, 'Sample Investment Management Request for Proposal'), how many copies of the proposal must be sent?
gold_answer: Ten (10) copies of the proposal and correspondence, sent to the pool administrator (shown as 'John Doe, 123 Main Street' in the template).
gold_passage: Please send ten (10) copies of your proposal and correspondence to:
notes: Template document with placeholders ([Name of JPA], [DATE], [TIME]); no real deadline or address. The phrase 'ten (10) copies' also appears in the SC RSIC general consultant RFP, so the question names the CAJPA sample.

question: What is the proposal deadline, and how many copies must be submitted, for the City of Madison (Florida) Police Officers' and Firefighters' Retirement System RFP No. 2025-0901 for investment consulting services?
gold_answer: Proposals must be received by 2:00 p.m. on September 1, 2025 at the City Clerk's office in Madison, FL (late proposals returned unopened); an original and five (5) copies must be submitted in a sealed envelope/package.
gold_passage: The Board must receive all proposals by 2:00 p.m. on September 1, 2025. | 1-3 Number of Copies: Proposers shall submit an original and five (5) copies.
notes: The street address is given as both '321 SW Rutledge Street' and '321 SE Rutledge Street' in the document; deadline and copies are consistent throughout.

question: In the Boston Retirement System's investment consulting services proposal questionnaire (Attachment 3), how many current public fund client references must be listed, and what minimum asset size must those clients have?
gold_answer: Up to 10 current public fund clients with assets greater than $1 billion for whom similar work was performed, giving name, contact, telephone number, asset values, number of years the client has retained the firm and the service used.
gold_passage: Provide a list of up to 10 current public fund clients with assets greater than $1 billion for whom work similar to that requested in this RFP has been performed by your firm.
notes: Attachment 3 is a separate file from the main BRS 2022 RFP (Boston_BRS__BRS_Inv_Consult_Serv_RFP_2022.pdf), which does not contain this requirement.

question: In the Illinois Firefighters' Pension Investment Fund (FPIF) February 2023 RFP for private markets investment consulting and discretionary OCIO advisory services, what long-term target allocation to private markets is FPIF building, and how is it split across asset classes?
gold_answer: A long-term target of 31% to private market asset classes: 10% private equity, 7% private debt, 10% real estate and 4% infrastructure. (FPIF seeks one non-discretionary consultant and approximately three discretionary OCIO advisors for this portfolio.)
gold_passage: The Consultant and Advisors will assist FPIF as the fund constructs its long-term target allocation of 31% to private market asset classes. FPIF has target allocations of 10% to private equity, 7% to private debt, 10% to real estate, and 4% to infrastructure.

question: In the Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois (TRS) FY25 RFP for private equity investment consultant services, what minimum private equity client experience must a firm certify?
gold_answer: The firm and/or its principals must have experience providing private equity consulting services to clients with, in aggregate, private equity portfolio assets of at least $10 billion.
gold_passage: The firm and/or its principals have experience providing private equity consulting services to clients, in aggregate, with private equity portfolio assets of at least $10 billion.
notes: Do not confuse with the TRS Illinois FY23 general investment consultant RFP, which requires combined client assets of at least $50 billion (existing question CONS-09).

question: A real assets investment consulting solicitation states that the funds' strategic asset allocation targets were adopted by the Board in 2003. As of September 30, 2010, how much did the Board have in its separate account private real estate program, its separate account private infrastructure program, and public real estate securities, and how large were its unfunded commitments?
gold_answer: About $164 million in the separate account private real estate program, $59 million in the separate account private infrastructure program, $25 million in public real estate securities, and about $88 million in unfunded commitments to real estate and infrastructure funds. Issuer: District of Columbia Retirement Board (Solicitation DCRB-2011-001); total Funds were over $4.2 billion.
gold_passage: As of September 30, 2010, the Board had approximately $164 million invested in a separate account private real estate investment program, $59 million in a separate account private infrastructure investment program, and $25 million in public real estate securities. | Additionally, the Board had approximately $88 million in unfunded commitments to real estate and infrastructure funds.
notes: Uniqueness checked: 'adopted by the Board in 2003' and '$164 million' appear only in the DCRB file.

question: In the published questions and answers for a city's pension fund consulting RFP, the city says it sent the RFP to 21 firms and last ran such a search in 2013. What does the plan currently pay for advisory services on its equities and for management of its fixed income?
gold_answer: $20K per year for advisory of the equity investments (about 70% of plan funds, held by Fiduciary Advisors); for the fixed income investments (about 30% of plan funds, held by Commerce Bank, the custodian and paying agent) 0.30% on the first $10M, 0.20% on the next $40M and 0.15% on the remaining balance. Issuer: City of Creve Coeur, MO.
gold_passage: $20K year for advisory of Equity investments (70% of Plan Funds) held by Fiduciary Advisors and .30% first $10M, .20% next $40M, and .15% on remaining balance for the Fixed investments (30% of Plan Funds)
notes: The fee information is only in the Q&A file, not in the main Creve Coeur RFP (which covers the same plan and is used by existing question CONS-15). '21 out' appears only in the Q&A file.

question: A sample investment management RFP for a domestic equity small cap growth mandate sets portfolio guidelines. What are the limits on single-issuer holdings, foreign issuers and cash, and which index must the portfolio outperform?
gold_answer: No more than 5% of the portfolio (at time of purchase) in any single issuer other than the Federal Government/Agencies or the designated cash reserve fund; no more than 20% in foreign issuers, which must trade on the NYSE, ASE or NASDAQ; cash and equivalents no more than 10% except during cash withdrawals or contributions; the portfolio is expected to outperform the Russell 2000 Growth Index, net of fees. Issuer: Illinois Municipal Retirement Fund (IMRF) sample RFP.
gold_passage: No more than 5% of the portfolio at time of purchase, will be invested in the securities of any single issuer | No more than 20% of the portfolio will be invested in securities of foreign issuers and these securities must be traded on the NYSE, ASE, or NASDAQ exchanges. | be no more than 10% of the portfolio except during periods of cash withdrawals or contributions. | The portfolio is expected to outperform the Russell 2000 Growth Index, net of fees.
notes: Other files mention 'small cap growth' only as an allocation line or asset class; the IMRF manager sample is the only small cap growth manager RFP. Its sibling IMRF consulting RFP has no such guidelines.

question: An investment manager RFP template for an emerging markets equity strategy (issued February 14, 2022, responses due March 31, 2022) lists required minimum qualifications and 'preferred criteria'. What live track record does it require, and what public pension client base does it prefer?
gold_answer: Required: an established (live) track record of at least 5 years managing the proposed emerging markets equity strategy (qualified women-, minority- or disabled-owned businesses are exempt). Preferred: at least two existing U.S. public pension fund clients with over $1 billion in total plan assets, or at least one existing public plan client with over $10 billion in total plan assets (plus no material litigation in the past five years). Issuer: State Universities Retirement System of Illinois (SURS).
gold_passage: The proposing firm must have an established (live) track record of at least 5 years managing the proposed emerging markets equity strategy | The firm has at least two existing U.S. public pension fund clients with over $1 billion in total plan assets, or at least one existing public plan as a client with over $10 billion in total plan assets.
notes: Template: firm-level AUM thresholds are left blank ('$__billion'), so they are not asked. The text extraction has stray 'Sample' watermark letters between lines.

question: An alternative investment consulting RFP describes a private equity portfolio of 225 holdings across 105 general partners. What are the approximate net asset values of the system's absolute return, private credit, private equity and real assets portfolios?
gold_answer: Absolute Return about $2.6 billion (11 funds across 10 managers); Private Credit about $1.8 billion (26 holdings, 16 GPs); Private Equity about $4.5 billion (225 holdings, 105 GPs); Real Assets about $3.1 billion (87 holdings, 58 GPs). Issuer: Indiana Public Retirement System (INPRS), RFP 23-09.
gold_passage: The Absolute Return portfolio net asset value is approximately $2.6 billion. | INPRS’s Private Credit portfolio currently consists of investments in 26 holdings across 16 general partners. The approximate net asset value of the portfolio is $1.8 billion. | INPRS’s Private Equity portfolio currently consists of investments in 225 holdings across 105 general partners. The approximate net asset value of the portfolio is $4.5 billion. | INPRS’s Real Assets portfolio currently consists of investments in 87 holdings across 58 general partners. The approximate net asset value of the portfolio is $3.1 billion.
notes: '225 holdings' appears only in the INPRS RFP 23-09 file (not in the INPRS core plus fixed income or audit RFPs).

question: In the Illinois Municipal Retirement Fund (IMRF) sample RFP for investment consulting, real estate consulting and performance measurement services, on what factors are respondents evaluated and ranked during the selection process?
gold_answer: Three factors: (1) Organization - stability, ownership, documented experience of key professionals; (2) Consulting Skill - investment philosophy, investment manager information collection and monitoring systems, risk management tools, performance measurement systems, and breadth of consulting expertise and experience; (3) Fees - consulting fees for services requested and associated costs.
gold_passage: Organization - stability, ownership, documented experience of key professionals | Consulting Skill - investment philosophy, investment manager information collection and monitoring systems, risk management tools, performance measurement systems and breadth of consulting expertise and experience. | Fees - Consulting fees for services requested and associated costs.
notes: Near-duplicate of the IMRF sample investment manager RFP (same template, same Part 8 wording), which uses four different factors (People, Process, Performance, Pricing).

question: In the Illinois Municipal Retirement Fund (IMRF) sample RFP for domestic equity small cap growth investment management, on what factors are respondents evaluated and ranked during the selection process?
gold_answer: Four primary factors: (a) People - stability of the organization, ownership structure and documented experience of key professionals; (b) Process - clearly defined, reasonable and repeatable investment strategy; (c) Performance - documented ability to meet investment performance benchmarks; (d) Pricing - fee schedule and associated costs.
gold_passage: (a) People - stability of the organization, ownership structure and documented experience of key professionals (b) Process - clearly defined, reasonable and repeatable investment strategy | (c) Performance - documented ability to meet investment performance benchmarks (d) Pricing - fee schedule and associated costs
notes: Near-duplicate of the IMRF sample investment consulting RFP, which uses three factors (Organization, Consulting Skill, Fees).

question: In the Massachusetts PRIM Board's October 2023 RFP for Multi-Asset Credit investment management services, what minimum total firm assets under management must a respondent have?
gold_answer: At least $10 billion in total firm assets under management, or alternatively at least $2 billion in multi-asset credit strategy assets under management, as of September 30, 2023.
gold_passage: The responding firm must have at least $10 billion in total firm assets under management, or the responding firm must have at least $2 billion in multi-asset credit strategy assets under management, as of September 30, 2023.
notes: File name is the generic 'PDF-Version-of-RFP'; it is the 2023 Multi-Asset Credit RFP. The 2026 PRIM Active Global Core Equity RFP has the same structure but requires $5 billion.

question: In the Massachusetts PRIM Board's September 2026 RFP for Active Global Core Equity investment management services, what minimum total firm assets under management must a respondent have?
gold_answer: At least $5 billion in total firm assets under management as of June 30, 2026.
gold_passage: The responding firm must have at least $5 billion in total firm assets under management as of June 30, 2026.
notes: Near-duplicate of the 2023 PRIM Multi-Asset Credit RFP ($10 billion total firm AUM or $2 billion in multi-asset credit AUM).

question: In the Baltimore City Employees' Retirement Systems (BCERS) RFP for an alternatives consultant, how many years must the proposing firm have been in business?
gold_answer: At least seven (7) years providing general consulting services plus private equity consulting services, or alternatives consulting services only (all minimum qualifications must be met as of November 8, 2024, 3:00 p.m. EDT).
gold_passage: The firm must have been in business for at least seven (7) or more years providing general consulting services plus private equity consulting services or alternatives consulting services only.
notes: BCERS and SBCERS RFPs share an almost identical template (Timeline box, FAQ 'What prompted the search?', 'Who is the incumbent consultant?'). SBCERS requires five years.

question: In the Santa Barbara County Employees' Retirement System (SBCERS) 2020 RFP for a discretionary private equity consultant, how many years must the proposing firm have been in business?
gold_answer: At least five (5) years providing services similar to those in the Scope of Services, measured as of December 31, 2020. (Separately, the organization must have provided investment management services for private equity transactions for five or more years.)
gold_passage: The Proposer must meet all of the following minimum qualifications as of December 31, 2020, | The firm must have been in business at least five (5) years providing services similar to those described in the Scope of Services section.
notes: Near-duplicate template of the Baltimore BCERS alternatives consultant RFP, which requires seven years. Avoid the SBCERS copies requirement: it is internally inconsistent ('seven (3) printed copies').

question: What evaluation criteria and weights does the Arizona Public Safety Personnel Retirement System (PSPRS) use in its RFP for non-discretionary investment consultant services?
gold_answer: 25% - relevant knowledge and experience in similar consulting engagements and current organizational capacity to provide experienced staff; 30% - quality and extent of the firm's capabilities in strategic advice, new investment identification and evaluation, operational due diligence, investment due diligence, manager performance reporting and monitoring, and back office support; 25% - demonstrated ability to meet service requirements (communicating with the CIO, investment team, Trustees and the Board's consultant, the operational plan, quality of assigned staff); 20% - overall cost of the proposed services.
gold_passage: 25 percent - Relevant knowledge and experience in similar consulting engagements, and current organizational capacity to provide experienced staff | 30 percent - Quality and extent of the firm’s capabilities regarding: | 25 percent - Demonstrated ability to meet service requirements | 20 percent - Overall cost of firm’s proposed services.

question: What is the full timetable in the City of York (Pennsylvania) Pension Funds' November 2016 RFP for an investment manager, adviser or consultant?
gold_answer: RFP issued November 28, 2016; questions due December 12, 2016; responses to questions posted December 16, 2016; proposals due January 6, 2017; interviewees notified February 17, 2017; interviews March 13-17, 2017; selected manager notified May 19, 2017; investment agreement signed June 16, 2017; mandate begins July 1, 2017.
gold_passage: RFP ISSUE DATE November 28, 2016 QUESTIONS RE RFP DUE December 12, 2016 RESPONSES TO QUESTIONS POSTED December 16, 2016 PROPOSALS DUE January 6, 2017 | INTERVIEWEES NOTIFIED February 17, 2017 INTERVIEWS March 13-17, 2017 NOTIFY SELECTED MANAGER May 19, 2017 SIGN INVESTMENT AGREEMENT June 16, 2017 BEGIN MANDATE July 1, 2017

question: Under the Baltimore City Employees' Retirement Systems (BCERS) alternatives consultant RFP, what must the consultant's quarterly performance report include at a minimum?
gold_answer: (i) market overview and outlook; (ii) allocation breakdown by geography, strategy and industry; (iii) update on each fund; (iv) listing of each fund by strategy; (v) date of commitment to each fund; (vi) commitment amount to each fund; (vii) drawdown amounts by fund; (viii) outstanding commitment by fund; (ix) distribution amounts by fund; (x) fund net asset values; (xi) IRR and multiples of each fund; (xii) items vi-xi aggregated for the core private equity portfolio, the specialized portfolio and the total portfolio.
gold_passage: Quarterly performance report to include at a minimum: i. Market overview and outlook ii. Allocation breakdown by geography, strategy and industry iii. Update on each fund iv. Listing of each fund by strategy v. Date of commitment to each fund | vi. Commitment amount to each fund vii. Drawdown amounts by fund viii. Outstanding commitment by fund ix. Distribution amounts by fund x. Fund net asset values xi. IRR and multiples of each fund | xii. Items vi through xi aggregated for the core private equity portfolio, specialized, portfolio, and total portfolio (core and specialized).
notes: Do not mix with the separate monthly report list (items i-vii) that immediately follows in the same section.

question: Which meetings must the investment consultant attend under the IMRF sample RFP for investment consulting, real estate consulting and performance measurement services, and how many days of meetings per year does IMRF estimate?
gold_answer: (1) Monthly IMRF Board meetings; (2) Investment Committee meetings; (3) the Annual IMRF Roundtable; (4) regional meetings with investment managers; (5) related investment meetings and discussions; (6) formal interviews with existing and potential investment managers; (7) ad hoc due diligence meetings with investment managers and staff. IMRF estimates about sixty days of meetings per year with the Board and/or staff, plus frequent telephone discussions with staff.
gold_passage: 1) Monthly IMRF Board meetings; 2) Investment Committee meetings; 3) Annual IMRF Roundtable; 4) Regional meetings with investment managers; | 5) Related investment meetings and discussions; 6) Formal interviews with existing and potential investment managers; 7) Ad hoc due diligence meetings with investment managers and Staff. | we estimate that there will be sixty days of meetings with the Board of Trustees and/or members of the staff held annually.

question: What selection criteria will the Evaluation Committee use to assess respondents to the Massachusetts PRIM Active Global Core Equity Investment Management Services RFP (September 2026)?
gold_answer: Ten criteria (not necessarily in order of importance or equally weighted): (1) organizational stability, ownership structure and experience of the firm; (2) experience, stability, depth and continuity of the proposed team; (3) clarity, consistency and repeatability of the investment philosophy and process, including consistency with the mandate; (4) historical track record and performance relative to the MSCI ACWI IMI across market cycles; (5) breadth and depth of research capabilities; (6) portfolio construction and risk management, including tracking error, active risk and exposures relative to the MSCI ACWI IMI; (7) capacity to manage the mandate in a separately managed account without degrading the strategy; (8) operational infrastructure; (9) quality and relevance of client references; (10) competitiveness of the proposed fees.
gold_passage: 1) Organizational stability, ownership structure, and experience of the firm. 2) Experience, stability, depth, and continuity of the team proposed to be dedicated to the PRIM account. | 4) Historical track record and performance relative to the MSCI ACWI IMI across market cycles. 5) Breadth and depth of research capabilities. | 8) Operational infrastructure. 9) Quality and relevance of client references. 10) Competitiveness of the proposed fees.
notes: The near-duplicate 2023 PRIM Multi-Asset Credit RFP lists nine shorter criteria (stability and experience of firm; team; philosophy and process; track record; research; risk management; operational infrastructure; client references; fee proposal) - do not confuse.

question: How do the private equity consultant RFPs in the corpus differ in the minimum experience they require of the primary (lead) consultant assigned to the account?
gold_answer: Hawaii ERS 2017 PE consultant RFP ad: primary consultant at least 7 years of domestic and international investment consulting/management experience with public pension plans. Hawaii ERS 2022 PE RFP: at least 7 years providing domestic and international private equity/debt consulting to public pension plans. SBCERS 2020 discretionary PE consultant RFP: at least one key professional with 10 years recommending PE investments for institutional clients, 3 of them with the current firm (plus key professionals with 5 years monitoring PE partnerships and 5 years reviewing partnership agreements). TRS Illinois FY25 PE consultant RFP: primary consultant with at least 3 years of PE investment consulting to pension funds, committing at least 20% of his or her time to TRS. Baltimore BCERS alternatives (PE-focused) consultant RFP: primary consultant with at least 5 years of consulting experience with DB public pension plans and at least 3 years with the firm. Related private-markets RFP: Missouri LAGERS requires a lead consultant with 5 years in a lead role recommending private market investments to U.S. public pension funds. Range: 3 years (TRS Illinois) to 10 years (SBCERS).
gold_passage: The primary consultant to be assigned to the ERS must have a minimum of seven years experience | The primary consultant assigned to the ERS account shall have a minimum of seven (7) years experience | must have a minimum of ten (10) years of experience (three (3) of which have been with the current firm) | Primary consultant proposed to be assigned to the TRS account has a minimum of three years of experience | must have a minimum of five (5) years of consulting experience with defined benefit public pension plans, and have been employed by the firm for at least three (3) years. | Lead consultant assigned to this account must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience in a lead role
notes: Scope: PE consultant RFPs (Hawaii 2017 ad, Hawaii 2022, SBCERS 2020, TRS Illinois FY25) plus the PE-focused Baltimore alternatives consultant RFP; LAGERS (private markets) included as related. Other private markets/alternatives/real assets RFPs: INPRS 23-09 primary consultants 5 years; FPIF lead consultant/CIO 10 years industry experience; DCRB senior consultant 10 years real assets; Hawaii 2022 real assets 7 years. Hawaii 2022 PE RFP is internally inconsistent on firm-level requirements (10 years / $5B in text vs 5 years / $3B in the certification form) but consistent on the 7-year primary consultant requirement.

question: What contract terms (initial length and any extension or renewal options) do the private equity, private markets, alternatives and real assets consultant RFPs in the corpus propose?
gold_answer: DC Retirement Board real assets (2011): 3-year original agreement. Hawaii ERS real assets (2022): about 3 years ending June 30, 2026, with a 3-year extension at ERS's option (to June 30, 2029). Hawaii ERS private equity (2022): 3 years with a 2-year extension at ERS's option. INPRS alternatives (RFP 23-09): initial 5 years, renewable at INPRS's option, total not to exceed 10 years. Missouri LAGERS private markets: initial 1 year, then an optional additional 2 years. TRS Illinois FY25 PE: from execution to December 31, 2029 (not to exceed five years), no extension. Arizona PSPRS non-discretionary (alternatives-focused) consultant: initial 3 years with two possible 1-year extensions. Baltimore BCERS, SBCERS 2020 PE and Illinois FPIF state no contract term.

notes: TRS Illinois term is in the sample agreement (Appendix F). Arizona passage continues 'year extensions before it will be bid again' on the next line. LAGERS continues '...right (but not the obligation) to enter into an agreement ... for period of an additional 2 years'.

question: Which of the private equity, alternatives and real assets consultant RFPs in the corpus identify the incumbent or existing consultants, who are they, and may the incumbent compete?
gold_answer: Baltimore BCERS alternatives consultant RFP: incumbent alternatives consultant is the Meketa Group, which may submit a proposal; the general consultant Marquette Associates may not. SBCERS 2020 PE consultant RFP: incumbent PE consultant is Hamilton Lane, invited to rebid. DC Retirement Board real assets RFP (2011): The Townsend Group is the incumbent specialist real assets consultant and is expected to respond; Meketa Investment Group (general consultant) is also expected to respond (Pantheon is the PE specialist). Arizona PSPRS non-discretionary consultant RFP: the Board's own fiduciary consultant NEPC is not up for bid (the procurement is for a consultant to the CIO and investment team). INPRS, FPIF, TRS Illinois FY25, LAGERS and the Hawaii RFPs do not name an incumbent.
gold_passage: The incumbent Alternatives Consultant is the Meketa Group. Meketa will be permitted to submit a proposal in this search. | Marquette will not be permitted to submit a proposal in this search. | SBCERS’ incumbent private equity consultant is Hamilton Lane. | Yes, the incumbent private equity consultant is invited to rebid. | Townsend Group, the incumbent specialist consultant, will continue to perform its fiduciary duties to the Funds throughout the search and selection process and is expected to respond to the RFP. | The Board contracts with its own consultant, NEPC, to serve as its fiduciary consultant; the Board’s consultant contract is not up for bid.
notes: DCRB text calls Meketa the 'generalist investment manager' in one sentence and 'general investment consultant' in another.
